A hole-in-one at a 1985 Illinois golf contest turned out to be a bribe ⛳

In the world of hole-in-one insurance, the fine print often matters more than the swing, and the shot of a lifetime can end up in a courtroom.

In June 1985, the son of the mayor of Oakbrook Terrace, Illinois teed off on the ninth hole at Country Lakes Country Club during a hole-in-one contest. An observer on the green pulled his ball from the cup, and he won his choice of a 1931 Cadillac or a $40,000 check.

According to the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals, the contest’s sponsor was a developer who needed the mayor’s support for a bond offering to finance an apartment complex. He palmed one of the golfer’s balls, put his hand in the cup, and displayed it. The court described the scheme as a payoff to the mayor, with the cost of the prize shifted to the National Hole-in-One Association, which provided the insurance.
